subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should this issue be split into the canonical backed-follow-up policy tracker plus a narrower exec/process-control bug, or kept as one coordinated Telegram agent reliability item?
rationale: The follow-up half overlaps the open product-policy decision in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58450, while the pkill abort half is a lower-level process-control behavior with a different likely fix path.

options.title: Split The Work
options.body: Track the reply-policy behavior under the canonical backed-follow-up issue and keep a narrower process-control issue for raw shell self-match versus managed `process(action="kill")` behavior.

options.title: Keep Coordinated
options.body: Keep this issue open as the coordinating item until maintainers define a single action-only Telegram invariant that also covers exec termination UX.

options.title: Re-check After Policy Lands
options.body: Wait for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58450 to land, then re-evaluate whether only the process-control surface remains.

recommendation.title: Split The Work
recommendation.body: Track the reply-policy behavior under the canonical backed-follow-up issue and keep a narrower process-control issue for raw shell self-match versus managed `process(action="kill")` behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest current blame signal across both checked surfaces and recent adjacent process/release termination work.
